limitations: The two direct captures retain randomized regex-map iteration and temporary input filenames; their executed assertion identities agree as a multiset, not as a byte-identical transcript.
Forty-two executed direct sites are a captured population, not proof that every source assertion was executed.
Exact ordered lists, snapshot equality, absence, regex absence and source/class-only predicates remain distinct; Java regex predicates are not evaluated in Python.
Direct records preserve actual checked values and JUnit identity, not inferred compiler options or submissions.
Corpus-only mode captures generated SQL programs instead of executing them; the separate rustFmt check executes formatting and Clippy.
The successful v8 Java capture has two JSON-string contains checks incorrectly tagged as structured snapshots; its strict-reader failure and the corrected v9 capture are both retained.

One shared calendar-window body differs only in relational allocation IDs between v7 and v9. A subsequent source repair has its own regression evidence; this frozen build is not relabeled as repaired.
Final template identity consolidation and Python runtime/platform accounting remain separate from capture completeness.
